Arithmetic with fractions

Source: R/arith.R
fraction-arithmetic.Rd

Results are exact, and in lowest terms. Whole numbers are fractions, but results are ordinary doubles if any element of a plain number isn't whole, as these are usually not exact. Use as_fraction() to convert them first.

Details

Arithmetic

+, -, *, /, %% and %/% are exact. ^ is exact if all exponents are whole numbers, and otherwise gives doubles. Inputs must be the same size, or size 1.

Summaries

sum(), prod(), mean(), median(), min(), max() and range() are exact. quantile() gives doubles.

Cumulative

cumsum(), cumprod(), cummin() and cummax() are exact.

Rounding

round(), floor(), ceiling() and trunc() are exact. round() gives the even digit for halves. signif() gives doubles.

Other functions

abs() and sign() give fractions. exp(), log(), sqrt() and so on give doubles.

If a result needs numbers too large for integers, all results are stored as doubles. Results which need numbers larger than 2^53 are missing, with a warning. Use as.double() to calculate approximately instead.

Logical operators (&, |, !, any(), all()) are not supported. Base R finds methods for functions like sum() with their first argument, so use sum(x, 1) instead of sum(1, x).

Examples

fraction(1, 3) + fraction(1, 6)
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 1/2
fraction(2, 3) * 2
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 4/3
fraction(2, 3)^-2
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 9/4

# Not all whole numbers
fraction(1, 2) + 0.25
#> [1] 0.75
fraction(1, 2) + as_fraction(0.25)
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 3/4

sum(fraction(1, 1:10))
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 7381/2520
cumsum(fraction(1, c(2, 4, 8)))
#> <fraction<double>[3]>
#> [1] 1/2 3/4 7/8
